$comment: Runnable example — WT_AUTH=none against a public site. Copy this, point it at your app, and replace the beats. `say` is tuned for the synthesizer (acronyms spelled out); `caption` is tuned for reading. Keep them separate.

beats.say: Start with the problem, not the architecture. Say what this software is for, in one sentence, before showing anything.
beats.caption: Lead with the problem, not the architecture.

beats.say: Point at what you are talking about. The cursor is drawn into the recording, so the viewer can follow your attention.
beats.caption: The cursor is drawn in — the viewer can follow your attention.

beats.say: A point action glides the cursor without clicking. A click action glides, ripples, then really clicks.
beats.caption: point = glide only · click = glide, ripple, then click.

beats.say: Scroll to bring the relevant part of the page into frame.
beats.caption: Scroll to frame what matters.

beats.say: Most beats do nothing at all. They hold the current view while you explain it. Use those to say the thing the visuals cannot carry on their own.
beats.caption: Most beats hold the view and let the narration carry the point.

action.title: When to use a card
bullets: Architecture, trade-offs, caveats — anything with no screen worth filming
A step too slow or too non-deterministic to record honestly
The closing summary of what works and what does not
Bullets reveal one at a time, in step with the narration

beats.say: A card draws a full screen panel inside the live page, revealing one bullet at a time.
beats.caption: A card: full-screen, revealed one bullet at a time.

beats.say: Use it when a step would be dishonest to film. A generation job that takes minutes and differs between runs is better described than staged.
beats.caption: Better described than staged.

beats.say: And use it to close. Say plainly what works and what does not. That is what makes the rest of the recording credible.
beats.caption: Close by saying plainly what works and what does not.

beats.say: If you find yourself narrating ninety seconds over a nearly empty screen, that is the signal to convert those beats to a card.
beats.caption: 90 seconds over an empty screen = convert it to a card.
